bottleneck: Cas proteins and their mRNAs are large cargos: packaging them efficiently into lipid nanoparticles or extracellular vesicles remains difficult, with low yields and hard purification. Natural tropism of vesicles is poorly controllable, and engineering precise targeting to specific infected or diseased cells in vivo is still nascent. Poor loading plus vague targeting means most CRISPR cargo never reaches its destination.
current_state: LNPs work well mainly for liver; extrahepatic delivery is an active research frontier. Exosome engineering shows promise but lacks scalable purification and targeting control.

sources.title: CRISPR Unleashed: Engineering Our Next-Gen Antivirals

title: CRISPR cargo too large for efficient nanoparticle delivery
why_it_blocks: Editing power is useless without delivery. Until non-viral carriers can load large editors and find the right cells, in vivo CRISPR stays confined to the liver and a few accessible tissues.
